# HEIC conversion

Source: https://filefn.com/docs/recipes/heic-conversion


Handle iPhone HEIC photos correctly in browsers, native iOS, and on the server — without any of them seeing HEIC.


# HEIC conversion

Goal: an upload pipeline that accepts HEIC inputs from iPhones and ends up with JPEG bytes everywhere downstream — no HEIC-decoding requirement on the server, no broken `<img>` tags in browsers.

## Browser

HEIC preprocessing is enabled by default, but conversion requires a supplied `converter` or a `globalThis.heic2any` implementation. FileFn does not bundle a decoder or infer universal browser HEIC support. Without a converter, HEIC uploads fail with `FILEFN_HEIC_CONVERSION_FAILED`.

Supply a decoder that produces a JPEG `Blob` (raw decoded pixels are not a JPEG):

```ts
import { createFileFnClient } from "@filefn/client";
import heic2any from "heic2any"; // Install separately; load this in browser-only code.

const client = createFileFnClient({
  baseUrl: "/filefn",
  preprocessing: {
    heic: {
      enabled: true,
      converter: async ({ file, targetMimeType, quality }) => {
        const output = await heic2any({ blob: file, toType: targetMimeType, quality });
        const jpeg = Array.isArray(output) ? output[0] : output;
        if (!jpeg) throw new Error("HEIC conversion produced no image");
        return jpeg;
      },
    },
  },
});
```

## iOS native

`FileFnForegroundUploader` and `FileFnBackgroundUploader` default to `FileFnHEICPreprocessor`:

```swift
let uploader = FileFnForegroundUploader(client: client)

let task = uploader.upload(
    FileFnForegroundUploadRequest(
        source: .photoAsset(asset),
        policy: "user-image"
    )
)

let result = try await task.value()
```

The preprocessor uses `CIImage` to transcode HEIC → JPEG before any bytes leave the app.

## Server side

The built-in `createImageTransformProcessor` accepts PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, and TIFF, not HEIC. Keep client preprocessing enabled when using this processor. After conversion, a supported JPEG upload can produce a preview:

```ts
import { createFileFn } from "@filefn/server";
import { createImageTransformProcessor } from "@filefn/processing";

const transform = createImageTransformProcessor({
  operations: [{ operation: "resize", options: { width: 2048, fit: "inside" }, suffix: "preview" }],
  outputFormat: "jpeg",
});
const fileFn = createFileFn({
  database, // Your configured database adapter.
  storage, // Your configured storage adapter.
  processing: { enabled: true, processors: [transform] },
});
```

To retain HEIC originals, supply a custom `Processor` that explicitly accepts `image/heic`/`image/heif`, decodes them using a HEIC-capable provider, and emits JPEG artifacts. Verify codec support in the deployed environment before disabling client preprocessing. Artifacts do not replace the stored original; original/full downloads remain HEIC.


---

# Image uploads

Source: https://filefn.com/docs/recipes/image-uploads


Production-grade image upload pipeline with HEIC handling, EXIF stripping, thumbnails, and previews.


# Image uploads

Goal: a single component that handles image uploads end to end:

- HEIC inputs converted to JPEG before upload.
- Two thumbnail sizes generated server-side.
- One preview-quality artifact for in-app rendering.
- JPEG-derived artifacts omit EXIF metadata; original bytes remain unchanged.

## Server policy

```ts
fileFn.definePolicy("user-image", {
  contentTypes: ["image/png", "image/jpeg", "image/webp"],
  maxSizeBytes: 25 * 1024 * 1024,
  visibility: "private",
  storageTarget: "durable",
  artifactStorageTarget: "hot-cdn",
  storagePath: ({ tenantId, fileId, versionId, fileName }) =>
    `tenants/${tenantId}/images/${fileId}/${versionId}/${fileName}`,
});
```

`maxSizeBytes` covers iPhone Live Photo size (10-15 MB) plus headroom.

## Server processors

```ts
import {
  createThumbnailProcessor,
  createImageTransformProcessor,
} from "@filefn/processing";

const thumbnails = createThumbnailProcessor({
  sizes: [
    { name: "thumb", width: 256, height: 256 },
    { name: "preview", width: 1024, height: 1024 },
  ],
  format: "jpeg",
  quality: 80,
});

// Sharp’s JPEG re-encode drops EXIF by default; this does not modify the original.
const normalise = createImageTransformProcessor({
  operations: [{ operation: "resize", options: { width: 2048, fit: "inside", withoutEnlargement: true }, suffix: "normalised" }],
  outputFormat: "jpeg",
  outputQuality: 85,
});

const fileFn = createFileFn({
  db, storage,
  processing: {
    enabled: true,
    processors: [normalise, thumbnails],
  },
});
```

## Client wiring

HEIC preprocessing is enabled by default, but you must supply a converter or `globalThis.heic2any`. Follow the [HEIC recipe](./heic-conversion) and handle conversion failures before uploading; the server processor only accepts supported image formats.

```ts
const handle = client.uploadFile({
  policy: "user-image",
  file,
});

const { fileId } = await handle.done();
```

## Rendering

```svelte
<script>
  import { onMount } from "svelte";
  import { client } from "$lib/client/filefn";

  let { fileId } = $props();
  let descriptor = $state(null);

  onMount(async () => {
    descriptor = await client.resolveRenderable({
      fileId,
      intent: "preview",
      preferLocal: true,
    });
  });
</script>

{#if descriptor?.state === "ready"}
  <img src={descriptor.source.url} alt="" />
{:else if descriptor?.state === "processing"}
  <Skeleton />
{:else if descriptor?.state === "pending-local"}
  <img src={descriptor.source.url} alt="" /> <!-- OPFS blob -->
{/if}
```

For thumbnail-quality rendering in lists, use `intent: "thumbnail"`. `intent: "full"` and download requests return original bytes. They do not inherit the derived artifacts’ metadata privacy properties.

## EXIF and privacy

`createImageTransformProcessor` supports only `resize`, `crop`, and `rotate`; there is no `strip-metadata` operation. Its Sharp JPEG re-encode drops EXIF by default. Consume the `transform-normalised` or thumbnail artifacts when this property is required, and verify their metadata in your processing environment. Original/full/download access still exposes the original bytes and any embedded metadata. Remove sensitive metadata before upload if the original itself must be safe to disclose.

## See also

- [Features › Processing](../features/processing).
- [Render intents](../core-concepts/render-intents).


---

# OPFS offline

Source: https://filefn.com/docs/recipes/opfs-offline


Reliable uploads when the network is bad — OPFS-staged content with automatic resume on reconnect.


# OPFS offline

Goal: a flaky-network-friendly upload that persists across tab reloads and resumes when the user reconnects.

## Enable

```ts
const client = createFileFnClient({
  baseUrl: "/filefn",
  offline: {
    enabled: true,
    partition: { serviceId: "app", principal: { kind: "user", principalId: session.userId } },
    // Who the live credentials act for now (another tab may have switched
    // accounts), read from local state: it is called offline too.
    currentPrincipal: () => readLocalSessionPrincipal(),
    // Credentials issued for exactly this principal (null when there are none).
    getAuthHeaders: (principal) => readHeadersFor(principal),
  },
});
```

That's it. Every `uploadFile(...)` call made offline:

1. Stages the bytes as a new generation in the user's partition of the durable queue.
2. Returns an `UploadHandle` whose `done()` waits for publication.
3. Is replayed when `navigator.onLine` becomes `true`, when another tab announces work, and on idle polls.

## Showing pending-local previews

```ts
const renderable = await client.resolveRenderable({
  fileId,
  intent: "preview",
  preferLocal: true,
});

if (renderable.state === "pending-local") {
  imgElement.src = (renderable.source as { url: string }).url; // blob: URL
}
```

## Listing pending uploads

```ts
const queue = client.getOfflineQueue();
for (const entry of await queue.list()) {
  console.log(entry.fileName, entry.size, entry.phase, entry.state, entry.attempts);
}
```

`list()` returns only this partition's entries and throws
`FILEFN_QUEUE_PRINCIPAL_MISMATCH` while another account is signed in. Useful
for an "uploads in progress" UI that survives reloads. Do not read the
pre-0.5 unscoped `OPFSStore` for this: it cannot see the partitioned journals,
and its records belong to no verified principal (see
[Features › Offline](../features/offline) for `listLegacyUploads` and
`migrateLegacyUpload`).

## Cancelling

```ts
const handle = client.uploadFile({ policy: "user-image", file });
handle.abort(); // removes OPFS row, cancels in-flight requests
```

## Quota

Before staging, check `navigator.storage.estimate()`:

```ts
const { quota = 0, usage = 0 } = await navigator.storage.estimate();
if (quota - usage < file.size) {
  // Skip OPFS — upload directly without offline persistence.
  // Or surface the issue and prompt the user to clear OPFS.
}
```

## Headless mode

If you want full control over when queued work runs (e.g. an Electron app),
turn implicit replay off and drive the partitioned queue with an explicit
`OfflineSync`:

```ts
const client = createFileFnClient({
  baseUrl: "/filefn",
  offline: { enabled: true, implicitReplay: false, partition, currentPrincipal, getAuthHeaders },
});

const sync = client.createOfflineSync({ onSyncError: (error, entryId) => report(error, entryId) });
sync.start();                               // online events, cross-tab wakeups, idle polls
await client.getOfflineQueue().process(id); // advance one entry now
sync.dispose();                             // or client.dispose(), which disposes it too
```

## See also

- [Features › Offline](../features/offline) — full reference.
- [Core Concepts › Offline](../core-concepts/offline) — design rationale.


---

# Processing container

Source: https://filefn.com/docs/recipes/processing-container


Run FileFn processing jobs in a container image with sharp, ffmpeg and tesseract, for example on Cloudflare Containers behind a queue consumer Worker.


# Processing container

`filefn/processing/container` builds a Node container image that runs queued `filefn.processing` jobs. A Worker that consumes the processing queue forwards each message to the container, which runs the FileFn processors that need native tools and records their artifacts.

```sh
# From the repository root. Cloudflare Containers run linux/amd64 images.
docker build --platform linux/amd64 -f filefn/processing/container/Dockerfile -t filefn-processing .
```

The image (`node:22-trixie-slim`) has `ffmpeg`, `tesseract` with English language data, and `sharp` compiled against Debian's libvips, which reads PDFs through poppler. It runs the `thumbnail`, `pdf-preview` and `ocr` processors (`FILEFN_PROCESSORS`); OCR calls the native `tesseract` command, and PDF previews are the rasterized first page (`metadata.renderMode: "page-rasterized"`). Audio and video processors are not offered yet.

## Routes

The container serves two routes and nothing else:

- `GET /health` returns `200 {"status":"ok"}`.
- `POST /jobs` takes `{"job": <queued message body>, "attempts": <delivery attempt>}` as `application/json`, runs the job through `createProcessingJobHandler`, and returns `200 {"outcome": …}`. Acknowledge the message unless `outcome.status` is `retry`. A request that arrives while `FILEFN_CONTAINER_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS` jobs are running waits up to `FILEFN_CONTAINER_JOB_WAIT_MS` (default 60 s) for a slot; after that it gets 503 with `Retry-After: 30`. A 503 or 500 asks for a delayed retry; a 400 or 413 body can never succeed.

`POST /jobs` requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with the `FILEFN_CONTAINER_TOKEN` value. The container refuses to start without a token unless `FILEFN_CONTAINER_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED=true` is set, which leaves `POST /jobs` open to anything that can reach the port.

The consumer retries with a delay, so a busy or failing container does not use up a message's attempts within seconds:

```ts
async queue(batch: MessageBatch, env: Env) {
  const container = env.FILEFN_PROCESSING_CONTAINER.getByName("processing");
  for (const message of batch.messages) {
    let response: Response;
    try {
      response = await container.fetch("http://container/jobs", {
        method: "POST",
        headers: { "content-type": "application/json", authorization: `Bearer ${env.FILEFN_CONTAINER_TOKEN}` },
        body: JSON.stringify({ job: message.body, attempts: message.attempts }),
      });
    } catch {
      message.retry({ delaySeconds: 30 });
      continue;
    }
    const outcome = response.ok ? ((await response.json()) as { outcome: { status: string } }).outcome : null;
    if (response.status === 400 || response.status === 413 || (outcome && outcome.status !== "retry")) message.ack();
    else message.retry({ delaySeconds: Number(response.headers.get("retry-after")) || 30 });
  }
}
```

Give the consumer `max_batch_size: 1`, a `max_concurrency` no higher than `FILEFN_CONTAINER_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS`, the same `max_retries` as `FILEFN_PROCESSING_MAX_RETRIES`, and a `dead_letter_queue`. The last delivery records `processing.failed` when it runs; if it cannot run (503, 500 or an unreachable container), the message lands in the dead-letter queue instead of disappearing.

## Storage and database

The container reaches storage through the R2 adapter: `FILEFN_R2_ACCOUNT_ID`, `FILEFN_R2_BUCKET`, `FILEFN_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `FILEFN_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` (or `FILEFN_R2_ENDPOINT` for an S3-compatible server such as MinIO).

`FILEFN_DATABASE` names the database: `memory` (tests and local runs only, since the producer cannot see it), or an ES module whose default export takes the environment and returns a `@superfunctions/db` adapter, such as a Drizzle adapter over your FileFn tables in Postgres. Add the module to an image built from this one. `FILEFN_NAMESPACE` and the processors must match the FileFn instance that enqueues the jobs.

The full list of variables, status codes and the test setup is in `filefn/processing/container/README.md`.

## What is verified

CI builds the image on Ubuntu, runs the container's suite inside it against MinIO with an in-memory database (a PNG thumbnail, the rasterized first page of a PDF and OCR through `tesseract`), and smoke-tests the runtime image. Live Cloudflare Containers are not covered.


---

# Signed share links

Source: https://filefn.com/docs/recipes/signed-share-links


Common share-link patterns — one-time, time-bound, password-protected, IP-restricted.


# Signed share links

filefn ships share links with TTLs and download caps. This recipe shows how to compose them with custom auth checks.

## One-time

```ts
const share = await fetch(`/filefn/${fileId}/share-links`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ maxDownloads: 1 }),
}).then((r) => r.json());

const shareUrl = `https://app.example.com/shares/${share.data.token}`;
```

The first download succeeds; the second returns `FILEFN_SHARE_DOWNLOADS_EXCEEDED`.

## Time-bound

```ts
await fetch(`/filefn/${fileId}/share-links`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    expiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString(), // 1 hour
  }),
});
```

## Auth-required (recipient must be logged in)

```ts
await fetch(`/filefn/${fileId}/share-links`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    requiresAuth: true,
    expiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString(),
  }),
});
```

The share token still gates access (recipients without it can't download), and on top of that recipients must present a valid filefn session.

## Password-protected

filefn doesn't ship a "password on share" feature. Compose one in your app:

```ts
// Your app DB, indexed by tokenHash
interface ShareGuard {
  tokenHash: string;
  passwordHash: string;
  attempts: number;
}

app.post("/shares/:token/check", async (c) => {
  const { password } = await c.req.json();
  const tokenHash = await hashToken(c.req.param("token"));
  const guard = await db.findOne("share_guards", { tokenHash });
  if (!guard) return c.json({ ok: false }, 404);
  if (!await bcrypt.compare(password, guard.passwordHash)) {
    return c.json({ ok: false }, 403);
  }
  // Cookie or session for the next request
  setShareSession(c, tokenHash);
  return c.json({ ok: true });
});
```

The actual filefn `/share-links/:token/download` call is gated by both your password check (your cookie) and filefn's token check.

## IP-restricted

Same idea — wrap the route with a custom proxy that records the IP at create time and rejects on mismatch.

## Tracking

`filefn_file_shares.downloads` tracks the count. Add a hook for analytics:

```ts
fileFn.events.on("share.downloaded", async (e) => {
  await analytics.record({
    fileId: e.fileId,
    shareTokenHashPrefix: e.tokenHashPrefix,
    at: Date.now(),
  });
});
```

(There's no `share.downloaded` event today — implement it via `redirect-aware` middleware on the share-download route, or add an emitter in your app.)

## See also

- [Features › Share links](../features/share-links).


---

# Tenant isolation

Source: https://filefn.com/docs/recipes/tenant-isolation


Per-tenant storage paths, quotas, grants, and authorization — the production isolation pattern.


# Tenant isolation

Goal: a single filefn instance serves many tenants, with clean separation at every layer (storage, DB rows, quotas, grants).

## Principal shape

The principal returned by `auth.resolveSession` should always carry `tenantId`:

```ts
{
  principalId: "user-123",
  tenantId: "tenant-acme",
  role: "org-admin",
}
```

All filefn rows are tagged with `tenantId`. Queries automatically scope by it.

## Storage path layout

```ts
fileFn.definePolicy("user-document", {
  contentTypes: ["application/pdf"],
  maxSizeBytes: 100 * 1024 * 1024,
  visibility: "private",
  storageTarget: "durable",
  artifactStorageTarget: "hot-cdn",
  storagePath: ({ tenantId, fileId, versionId, fileName }) =>
    `tenants/${tenantId}/docs/${fileId}/${versionId}/${fileName}`,
});
```

Every storage object lives under `tenants/<tenantId>/`. If you front it with a CDN, configure cache keys to include the tenant prefix to keep tenant data isolated at the cache layer too.

For multiple buckets, register named adapters with `createRoutedStorageAdapter({ adapters, defaultTarget })` and assign trusted policies to those targets. The router has no `resolveTarget` callback. Keep tenant authorization in the host and do not accept an arbitrary adapter/target from the client. See [CDN and storage routing](/docs/recipes/cdn-integration).

## Quotas

```ts
const quota: QuotaProvider = {
  async check({ tenantId, requested }) {
    const plan = await loadTenantPlan(tenantId!);
    const used = await sumStorageUsedFor(tenantId!);
    return {
      allowed: used + requested <= plan.maxBytes,
      current: used,
      limit: plan.maxBytes,
    };
  },
  async used({ tenantId }) {
    const plan = await loadTenantPlan(tenantId!);
    const used = await sumStorageUsedFor(tenantId!);
    return { current: used, limit: plan.maxBytes };
  },
};

const fileFn = createFileFn({ db, storage, quota });
```

## Authorizer

```ts
import { composeAuthorizers, createDefaultAuthorizer } from "@filefn/server";
import type { AuthorizerStrategy } from "@filefn/server";

const orgWideRead: AuthorizerStrategy = {
  async canRead(file, principal) {
    if (principal.tenantId !== file.tenantId) return false; // hard cross-tenant block
    if (principal.role === "org-admin") return true;
    return undefined; // defer
  },
  async canDelete(file, principal) {
    if (principal.tenantId !== file.tenantId) return false;
    if (principal.role === "org-admin") return true;
    return undefined;
  },
};

const authorizer = composeAuthorizers([
  orgWideRead,
  createDefaultAuthorizer({ db, namespace: "filefn" }),
]);

const fileFn = createFileFn({ db, storage, quota, authorizer });
```

The cross-tenant `false` short-circuits — even if the file's `ownerId` matches `principalId` (it shouldn't), the explicit tenant check denies.

## Share links across tenants

By default, share links are public — anyone with the token can download (subject to TTL / cap / `requiresAuth`). To prevent cross-tenant sharing entirely, refuse to mint share links for files outside the principal's tenant — but the kernel already does this through the authorizer's `canShare` check.

## Multi-tenant rate limiting

```ts
import { createRateLimiter } from "@superfunctions/middleware";

const limiter = createRateLimiter({
  windowMs: 60_000,
  maxRequests: 1000,
  keyResolver: (request, ctx) => ctx.principal?.tenantId ?? `ip:${ctx.ip}`,
  persistence: redisPersistence,
});

const fileFn = createFileFn({ db, storage, rateLimiter: limiter });
```

Now each tenant has its own bucket, and unauthenticated requests fall back to per-IP buckets.

## See also

- [Core Concepts › Visibility](../core-concepts/visibility) — public / private / shared.
- [Features › Quota](../features/quota) — quota provider authoring.
- [Features › Grants](../features/grants) — per-tenant role-based access.


---

# Video uploads

Source: https://filefn.com/docs/recipes/video-uploads


Large-file video uploads with 720p transcoding, poster frames, and queued processing.


# Video uploads

Goal:

- Multi-GB uploads survive network blips.
- Poster frame at 1s.
- A 720p transcode; adaptive multi-resolution playback requires a custom processor.
- Processing happens off the request path (queued).

## Policy

```ts
fileFn.definePolicy("user-video", {
  contentTypes: ["video/mp4", "video/quicktime", "video/webm"],
  maxSizeBytes: 5 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024,    // 5 GiB
  visibility: "private",
  storageTarget: "durable",
  artifactStorageTarget: "hot-cdn",
  storagePath: ({ tenantId, fileId, versionId, fileName }) =>
    `tenants/${tenantId}/videos/${fileId}/${versionId}/${fileName}`,
});
```

## Processors (queued)

```ts
import {
  createVideoProcessor,
  createCommandVideoProvider,
} from "@filefn/processing";
import { createFlowFnProvider } from "@flowfn/server";

const flowFn = createFlowFnProvider({
  /* queue + worker config */
});

const video = createVideoProcessor({
  provider: createCommandVideoProvider({ ffmpegPath: "ffmpeg" }),
  posterOptions: { timestamp: 1.0, width: 1024 },
  transcode: true,
  transcodeOptions: { resolution: "720p", codec: "h264", bitrate: "2M" },
});

const fileFn = createFileFn({
  db, storage,
  processing: {
    enabled: true,
    processors: [video],
    flowFn, // dispatch processing to a worker
  },
});
```

The worker pulls jobs, runs the processor, and writes artifacts back. The user's upload request returns the moment the bytes finish — they don't wait for a 5-minute transcode.

## Client UX

```ts
const handle = client.uploadFile({
  policy: "user-video",
  file,
});

handle.onProgress(({ bytesUploaded, bytesTotal }) => {
  setProgress((bytesUploaded / bytesTotal) * 100);
});

const result = await handle.done();
// result.fileId, result.versionId — file is uploaded; processing in flight
```

After the upload returns, poll `client.resolveRenderable({ fileId, intent: "preview" })`:

- Initial state: `state: "processing"` — show a "preparing your video" placeholder.
- After transcode: `state: "ready"` — show the poster frame, then the player.

## Adaptive playback

For HLS / DASH, run a custom processor that wraps `ffmpeg` to emit segmented manifests, and store them as separate artifacts (`hls-master`, `hls-720p-segment-N`). Render the master URL in your player.

## Resilience

OPFS offline (`offline.enabled: true`) and `client.resumeUpload` give you "user closed the laptop in the middle of a 4 GiB upload, woke up, finished" semantics out of the box.

## See also

- [Features › Processing](../features/processing).
- [Recipes › OPFS offline](./opfs-offline).


---

# Virus scanning

Source: https://filefn.com/docs/recipes/virus-scanning


Plug ClamAV (or any AV provider) into the filefn processing pipeline as a custom processor.


# Virus scanning

Goal: every uploaded file is scanned for malware before it's served. Infected files are quarantined.

## Processor

```ts
import type { Processor, ProcessorResult } from "@filefn/processing";
import { exec } from "node:child_process";
import { writeFile, unlink } from "node:fs/promises";
import { promisify } from "node:util";

const execP = promisify(exec);

export function createClamAVProcessor(): Processor {
  return {
    name: "clamav",
    supportedMimeTypes: ["*/*"],
    async process(input, getData): Promise<ProcessorResult> {
      const data = await getData();
      const tmpPath = `/tmp/filefn-${input.fileId}-${input.versionId}`;
      await writeFile(tmpPath, data);

      try {
        await execP(`clamscan --no-summary "${tmpPath}"`);
        return {
          success: true,
          artifacts: [
            {
              kind: "av-scan",
              mimeType: "application/json",
              data: new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify({
                clean: true,
                scannedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
              })),
              storageKey: input.storageKey + ".av-scan.json",
            },
          ],
        };
      } catch (error) {
        // clamscan exits non-zero on detection
        return {
          success: false,
          error: "av-scan-failed",
          artifacts: [
            {
              kind: "av-scan",
              mimeType: "application/json",
              data: new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify({
                clean: false,
                detection: String(error),
                scannedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
              })),
              storageKey: input.storageKey + ".av-scan.json",
            },
          ],
        };
      } finally {
        await unlink(tmpPath).catch(() => {});
      }
    },
  };
}
```

## Wire it

```ts
const fileFn = createFileFn({
  db, storage,
  processing: {
    enabled: true,
    processors: [createClamAVProcessor() /* + others */],
  },
});
```

## Quarantine

When `processing.failed` fires with the `clamav` processor name, mark the file in your app as quarantined:

```ts
fileFn.events.on("processing.failed", async (event) => {
  if (event.processor === "clamav") {
    await db.update("filefn_files", { metadata: { quarantined: true } }, { fileId: event.fileId });
    await alertTeam({ fileId: event.fileId, reason: "av-scan-failed" });
  }
});
```

Add a custom `Authorizer` that denies reads for quarantined files:

```ts
const quarantineGuard: AuthorizerStrategy = {
  async canRead(file) {
    if (file.metadata?.quarantined) return false;
    return undefined;
  },
};
```

## Async scanning

For multi-GB files, run scanning via `@flowfn/server` so the upload request returns immediately. The user can be told "your file is being scanned" and the UI polls the renderable until it's safe to render.

## See also

- [Recipes › Custom processor](./custom-processor) — the general pattern.


---

# Workers with AuthFn, R2 and Queues

Source: https://filefn.com/docs/recipes/workers-authfn-r2-queues


A complete Cloudflare Worker that serves AuthFn and FileFn on one origin, stores files in a regional R2 bucket, keeps metadata in the region's Postgres, and processes uploads on the device or through Cloudflare Queues and a processing container.


# Workers with AuthFn, R2 and Queues

This recipe puts the pieces from [Cloudflare Workers](./cloudflare-workers) and [Processing container](./processing-container) together in one Worker:

- **AuthFn** serves `/auth/*` and authenticates every FileFn request, with CSRF checks for cookie sessions.
- **FileFn** serves `/files/*`. File objects go to the region's **R2** bucket and file metadata to the FileFn tables in the region's **Postgres**.
- **Processing** runs on the device (clients upload their own thumbnails) or remotely (a **Queue** carries each job to the processing container), chosen per environment.

Deploy one Worker per region. Each region has its own R2 bucket, Postgres database, queue and container, so a file's bytes and metadata are stored in its region. Where they are processed is a separate question: Cloudflare runs the Worker wherever the request arrives, and nothing in this recipe restricts where the processing container runs, so with `remote` processing the container may read a file's bytes outside its region. If bytes must not leave the region while processed, use `device` processing, or a placement control you have verified for your account.

```jsonc
// wrangler.jsonc
{
  "name": "files-api",
  "main": "src/worker.ts",
  "compatibility_date": "2025-11-13",
  "compatibility_flags": ["nodejs_compat"],
  "triggers": { "crons": ["*/15 * * * *"] },
  "env": {
    "eu": {
      "routes": [
        { "pattern": "app.example.eu/auth/*", "zone_name": "example.eu" },
        { "pattern": "app.example.eu/files/*", "zone_name": "example.eu" }
      ],
      "vars": { "R2_BUCKET": "files-eu", "R2_JURISDICTION": "eu", "FILEFN_PROCESSING": "remote" },
      "hyperdrive": [{ "binding": "HYPERDRIVE", "id": "<eu Hyperdrive config ID>" }],
      "queues": {
        "producers": [{ "binding": "FILEFN_PROCESSING_QUEUE", "queue": "filefn-processing-eu" }],
        "consumers": [{
          "queue": "filefn-processing-eu",
          "max_batch_size": 1,
          "max_concurrency": 2, // At most the container's FILEFN_CONTAINER_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS.
          "max_retries": 3, // The container's FILEFN_PROCESSING_MAX_RETRIES.
          "dead_letter_queue": "filefn-processing-eu-dlq"
        }]
      },
      "containers": [{
        "class_name": "ProcessingContainer",
        // The processing container image plus your FILEFN_DATABASE module, pushed with `wrangler containers push`.
        "image": "registry.cloudflare.com/<account ID>/filefn-processing:1",
        "max_instances": 1
      }],
      "durable_objects": {
        "bindings": [{ "name": "FILEFN_PROCESSING_CONTAINER", "class_name": "ProcessingContainer" }]
      }
    }
  },
  "migrations": [{ "tag": "v1", "new_sqlite_classes": ["ProcessingContainer"] }]
}
```

Set `R2_ACCOUNT_ID`, `R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `FILEFN_CONTAINER_TOKEN` and `CONTAINER_DATABASE_URL` as secrets for each environment (`wrangler secret put R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID --env eu`). Leave out the queue, container and Durable Object bindings in an environment that sets `FILEFN_PROCESSING` to `device`.

Build the image as the [processing container](./processing-container) recipe shows, add a `db.mjs` (the `FILEFN_DATABASE` module from the container's README, which connects with `DATABASE_URL`) to an image derived from it, and push that image. Hyperdrive serves only Workers, so the container connects to the region's Postgres directly with `CONTAINER_DATABASE_URL`.

The browser uploads parts straight to R2 with signed URLs, so the bucket needs a CORS rule for the app's origin. The client reads each part's `ETag` and sends `x-upload-session-token` with the part:

```json
{
  "rules": [{
    "allowed": {
      "origins": ["https://app.example.eu"],
      "methods": ["PUT", "GET"],
      "headers": ["content-type", "x-upload-session-token"]
    },
    "exposeHeaders": ["ETag"],
    "maxAgeSeconds": 3600
  }]
}
```

Apply it with `wrangler r2 bucket cors set files-eu --file r2-cors.json --jurisdiction eu`. `GET` lets the page `fetch` signed download URLs; an `<img>` without `crossorigin` does not need it.

In a `remote` environment, `ProcessingContainer` (below) starts the region's processing container with these variables, which must agree with this Worker and its queue consumer:

| Container variable | Must be |
| --- | --- |
| `FILEFN_R2_BUCKET`, `FILEFN_R2_ACCOUNT_ID` | The Worker's `R2_BUCKET` and `R2_ACCOUNT_ID`. |
| `FILEFN_R2_JURISDICTION` | The Worker's `R2_JURISDICTION` (`eu` here). Without it the container addresses the bucket outside its jurisdiction and cannot read the uploads. |
| `FILEFN_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `FILEFN_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | A token that can read and write this bucket. |
| `FILEFN_DATABASE`, `DATABASE_URL` | `./db.mjs` in the image, and the Worker's `CONTAINER_DATABASE_URL`: the same regional Postgres. |
| `FILEFN_NAMESPACE` | The FileFn namespace of `createFiles` below (FileFn's default here, so leave both unset). |
| `FILEFN_PROCESSORS` | The names in `containerProcessors` below (`thumbnail,pdf-preview,ocr`). |
| `FILEFN_PROCESSING_MAX_RETRIES` | The consumer's `max_retries` (3). |
| `FILEFN_CONTAINER_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS` | At least the consumer's `max_concurrency` (2); otherwise extra deliveries wait, get 503 and use up their attempts. |
| `FILEFN_CONTAINER_TOKEN` | The Worker's `FILEFN_CONTAINER_TOKEN` secret. |

## Environment

```ts
// src/env.ts
export interface Env {
  /** This region's Postgres, which holds the AuthFn and FileFn tables. */
  HYPERDRIVE: Hyperdrive;
  R2_ACCOUNT_ID: string;
  /** This region's bucket. */
  R2_BUCKET: string;
  R2_JURISDICTION?: "eu" | "fedramp";
  R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID: string;
  R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: string;
  /** `device`: clients upload their own artifacts. `remote`: the queue and the container process uploads. */
  FILEFN_PROCESSING: "device" | "remote";
  FILEFN_PROCESSING_QUEUE?: Queue;
  FILEFN_PROCESSING_CONTAINER?: DurableObjectNamespace;
  FILEFN_CONTAINER_TOKEN?: string;
  /** The region's Postgres for the container, which cannot use Hyperdrive. */
  CONTAINER_DATABASE_URL?: string;
}
```

`createDatabase(env)` in `src/database.ts` is your `@superfunctions/db` adapter over the region's Postgres, for example the [PostgreSQL adapter](../adapters/db-postgres) with `pg` connecting through `env.HYPERDRIVE.connectionString`. AuthFn and FileFn share it, so its table registry must include both libraries' tables, and their migrations must have run (see [DB adapters](../adapters/db)).

## AuthFn

```ts
// src/auth.ts
import {
  authfn,
  authFnPlugins,
  AuthFnCsrfInvalidError,
  AuthFnError,
  defineAuthFnScopes,
  hasScopes,
  type AuthFnServer,
  type AuthFnSession,
} from "authfn";
import { authFnApiKeyPlugin } from "@authfn/api-keys";
import { authFnPasswordPlugin } from "@authfn/password";
import { forbidden, type FileFnPrincipal } from "@filefn/server";
import type { Adapter } from "@superfunctions/db";

/** The scopes an AuthFn API key can be granted for FileFn. */
export const scopes = defineAuthFnScopes({ files: ["read", "write"] });

export const authApp = authfn({
  basePath: "/auth",
  scopes,
  plugins: authFnPlugins(authFnPasswordPlugin(), authFnApiKeyPlugin()),
});

export function createAuth(database: Adapter): AuthFnServer {
  return authApp.createServer({ database });
}

const SAFE_METHODS = new Set(["GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS"]);

/** FileFn's `auth.resolveSession`: the AuthFn session as a FileFn principal. */
export async function resolveFileFnPrincipal(auth: AuthFnServer, request: Request): Promise<FileFnPrincipal | null> {
  let session: AuthFnSession | null;
  try {
    session = SAFE_METHODS.has(request.method)
      ? await auth.provider.authenticate(request)
      : await auth.authorizeMutation(request);
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof AuthFnCsrfInvalidError) throw forbidden({ reason: "csrf" });
    if (error instanceof AuthFnError && error.status === 401) return null;
    throw error;
  }
  if (!session) return null;
  // User sessions carry ["*"]; an API-key session carries only its key's scopes.
  const needed = SAFE_METHODS.has(request.method) ? "files:read" : "files:write";
  if (!hasScopes(session, needed, { registry: scopes })) throw forbidden({ reason: "scope", missingScopes: [needed] });
  return { principalId: session.actorId, tenantId: session.tenantId };
}
```

- Reads (`GET`, `HEAD`) accept a cookie session, a bearer session token or an API key.
- Every other method goes through `authorizeMutation`, which requires the `x-authfn-csrf` header to match the `authfn.csrf` cookie when the request carries a session cookie. A request without a valid credential resolves to no principal, so FileFn answers `401 FILEFN_AUTH_REQUIRED`. A CSRF mismatch answers `403 FILEFN_FORBIDDEN`. Any other error, such as a database failure, is not turned into a 401.
- AuthFn accepts an API key in any `Authorization` header, so the scope check applies to every session. Cookie and bearer user sessions carry the `*` scope and pass. An API-key session passes only with `files:read` (or `files:*`) for reads and `files:write` (or `files:*`) for everything else; a key without the needed scope, including a key created without scopes, gets `403 FILEFN_FORBIDDEN` and never the owner's access. The `@authfn/api-keys` plugin adds the `api_keys` table to AuthFn's schema and lets a signed-in user create keys with `POST /auth/api-keys` and a body such as `{"name":"sync","scopes":["files:read"]}`; scopes outside `scopes` are rejected.
- A user's session or a user-owned API key that passes the scope check acts as the user (`actorId` is the user ID). An unowned service key acts as itself (`actorId` is the key ID). Set up FileFn [policies](../core-concepts/policies) and [grants](../features/grants) for those principals.

## FileFn

```ts
// src/filefn.ts
import { createFileFn, type FileFn, type FileFnConfig, type Processor } from "@filefn/server";
import { createCloudflareFlowFnProvider } from "@filefn/processing/queues/cloudflare";
import { createR2StorageAdapter } from "@superfunctions/storage-r2";
import type { Adapter } from "@superfunctions/db";
import type { AuthFnServer } from "authfn";
import { resolveFileFnPrincipal } from "./auth";
import type { Env } from "./env";

// The processors the container runs (its FILEFN_PROCESSORS). The Worker only enqueues jobs
// for them; the container decides which apply to a file and runs them.
const containerProcessors: Processor[] = ["thumbnail", "pdf-preview", "ocr"].map((name) => ({
  name,
  supportedMimeTypes: ["*/*"],
  async process() {
    throw new Error(`${name} runs in the processing container, not in the Worker`);
  },
}));

function processingFor(env: Env): FileFnConfig["processing"] {
  if (env.FILEFN_PROCESSING === "device") return { enabled: false };
  if (!env.FILEFN_PROCESSING_QUEUE) throw new Error("FILEFN_PROCESSING=remote needs the FILEFN_PROCESSING_QUEUE binding");
  return {
    enabled: true,
    processors: containerProcessors,
    flowFn: createCloudflareFlowFnProvider({ "filefn.processing": env.FILEFN_PROCESSING_QUEUE }),
  };
}

export function createFiles(env: Env, ctx: ExecutionContext, database: Adapter, auth: AuthFnServer): FileFn {
  return createFileFn({
    database,
    storage: createR2StorageAdapter({
      accountId: env.R2_ACCOUNT_ID,
      bucket: env.R2_BUCKET,
      jurisdiction: env.R2_JURISDICTION,
      accessKeyId: env.R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID,
      secretAccessKey: env.R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY,
    }),
    basePath: "/files",
    runtime: { defer: (work) => ctx.waitUntil(work) },
    auth: {
      required: true,
      resolveSession: (request) => resolveFileFnPrincipal(auth, request),
    },
    policies: [{ name: "photos", contentTypes: ["image/*"], maxSizeBytes: 25 * 1024 * 1024, visibility: "private" }],
    processing: processingFor(env),
  });
}
```

FileFn is created per request so that `runtime.defer` uses that request's `ctx.waitUntil`; see [Cloudflare Workers](./cloudflare-workers) for the base path, background work and rate-limit rules that come with that.

With `FILEFN_PROCESSING: "remote"`, every completed upload enqueues one `filefn.processing` job. Keep the processor names equal to the container's `FILEFN_PROCESSORS` and its `FILEFN_NAMESPACE` equal to this FileFn's namespace (the table above lists every container variable that must match). With `device`, server processing is off and clients upload thumbnails and converted images with `uploadArtifact` (below).

## Processing container

```ts
// src/processing-container.ts
import { DurableObject } from "cloudflare:workers";
import type { Env } from "./env";

const PORT = 8080;

/** Starts the region's processing container and forwards the queue consumer's requests to it. */
export class ProcessingContainer extends DurableObject<Env> {
  private ready: Promise<void> | undefined;

  async fetch(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
    const container = this.ctx.container;
    if (!container) throw new Error("ProcessingContainer needs a containers entry in wrangler.jsonc");
    if (!container.running) {
      container.start({ enableInternet: true, env: containerEnv(this.env) });
      this.ready = undefined;
    }
    this.ready ??= waitUntilHealthy(container);
    try {
      await this.ready;
    } catch (error) {
      this.ready = undefined;
      throw error;
    }
    return container.getTcpPort(PORT).fetch(request);
  }
}

function containerEnv(env: Env): Record<string, string> {
  if (!env.FILEFN_CONTAINER_TOKEN || !env.CONTAINER_DATABASE_URL) {
    throw new Error("the processing container needs FILEFN_CONTAINER_TOKEN and CONTAINER_DATABASE_URL");
  }
  return {
    FILEFN_R2_ACCOUNT_ID: env.R2_ACCOUNT_ID,
    FILEFN_R2_BUCKET: env.R2_BUCKET,
    ...(env.R2_JURISDICTION ? { FILEFN_R2_JURISDICTION: env.R2_JURISDICTION } : {}),
    FILEFN_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID: env.R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID,
    FILEFN_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: env.R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY,
    FILEFN_DATABASE: "./db.mjs",
    DATABASE_URL: env.CONTAINER_DATABASE_URL,
    FILEFN_PROCESSORS: "thumbnail,pdf-preview,ocr",
    FILEFN_PROCESSING_MAX_RETRIES: "3",
    FILEFN_CONTAINER_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS: "2",
    FILEFN_CONTAINER_TOKEN: env.FILEFN_CONTAINER_TOKEN,
  };
}

/** Waits up to 30 seconds for the container's `GET /health`. */
async function waitUntilHealthy(container: Container): Promise<void> {
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 60; attempt += 1) {
    try {
      if ((await container.getTcpPort(PORT).fetch("http://container/health")).ok) return;
    } catch {
      // Not listening yet.
    }
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 500));
  }
  throw new Error("the processing container did not become healthy within 30 seconds");
}
```

The Durable Object runs one container instance (`getByName("processing")` in the consumer below) and starts it again after it stops.

## Worker

```ts
// src/worker.ts
import { createAuth } from "./auth";
import { createDatabase } from "./database";
import type { Env } from "./env";
import { createFiles } from "./filefn";

export { ProcessingContainer } from "./processing-container";

function isUnder(pathname: string, prefix: string): boolean {
  return pathname === prefix || pathname.startsWith(`${prefix}/`);
}

export default {
  async fetch(request, env, ctx) {
    const database = createDatabase(env);
    const auth = createAuth(database);
    const { pathname } = new URL(request.url);
    if (isUnder(pathname, "/auth")) return auth.router.handle(request);
    const response = await createFiles(env, ctx, database, auth).router.handle(request);
    return response ?? new Response("Not found", { status: 404 });
  },

  // Forwards each processing job to the container (see the processing container recipe).
  async queue(batch, env) {
    const token = env.FILEFN_CONTAINER_TOKEN;
    if (!env.FILEFN_PROCESSING_CONTAINER || !token) {
      throw new Error("the queue consumer needs FILEFN_PROCESSING_CONTAINER and FILEFN_CONTAINER_TOKEN");
    }
    const container = env.FILEFN_PROCESSING_CONTAINER.getByName("processing");
    for (const message of batch.messages) {
      let response: Response;
      try {
        response = await container.fetch("http://container/jobs", {
          method: "POST",
          headers: { "content-type": "application/json", authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
          body: JSON.stringify({ job: message.body, attempts: message.attempts }),
        });
      } catch {
        message.retry({ delaySeconds: 30 });
        continue;
      }
      const outcome = response.ok ? ((await response.json()) as { outcome: { status: string } }).outcome : null;
      if (response.status === 400 || response.status === 413 || (outcome && outcome.status !== "retry")) message.ack();
      else message.retry({ delaySeconds: Number(response.headers.get("retry-after")) || 30 });
    }
  },

  async scheduled(_controller, env, ctx) {
    const database = createDatabase(env);
    await createFiles(env, ctx, database, createAuth(database)).cleanupExpiredSessions();
  },
} satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;
```

The consumer retries a job whose request failed, after 30 seconds. The container finishes a job it has started even if the request is cut off, so a redelivery can run the same job while the first run is still going. FileFn allows this: artifact rows have IDs derived from the file, version and kind, so overlapping runs record one artifact set (the `@filefn/server` suite runs two deliveries of a job at once), and a delivery after a completed run returns `duplicate`. The cost is repeated processor work, and `processing.completed` can be emitted once per run, so make its listeners idempotent.

AuthFn's router already includes its `/auth` base path. Because both mounts share the app's origin, the browser sends the AuthFn session cookie to `/files` without CORS.

## Browser client

```ts
// src/files-client.ts (browser)
import { createFileFnClient } from "@filefn/client";

function cookie(name: string): string | undefined {
  const prefix = `${name}=`;
  const entry = document.cookie.split("; ").find((part) => part.startsWith(prefix));
  return entry === undefined ? undefined : decodeURIComponent(entry.slice(prefix.length));
}

export const files = createFileFnClient({
  baseUrl: `${location.origin}/files`,
  // Sent with every request, including proxy part uploads, so cookie sessions pass AuthFn's CSRF check.
  getAuthHeaders: (): Record<string, string> => {
    const csrf = cookie("authfn.csrf");
    return csrf ? { "x-authfn-csrf": csrf } : {};
  },
});

const THUMBNAIL_TYPES = new Set(["image/jpeg", "image/png", "image/webp"]);

/** Uploads a photo and, with FILEFN_PROCESSING=device, the thumbnail the device made. Returns the file ID. */
export async function uploadPhoto(photo: File, thumbnail?: Blob): Promise<string> {
  // Checked before the photo is uploaded: a Blob from canvas.toBlob or fetch can have an empty type.
  if (thumbnail && !THUMBNAIL_TYPES.has(thumbnail.type)) {
    throw new TypeError(`thumbnail type must be one of ${[...THUMBNAIL_TYPES].join(", ")}, not "${thumbnail.type}"`);
  }
  const upload = files.uploadFile({ policy: "photos", file: photo });
  const { fileId, versionId } = await upload.done();
  if (thumbnail) {
    try {
      await files.uploadArtifact({ fileId, versionId, kind: "thumbnail-medium", data: thumbnail, mimeType: thumbnail.type });
    } catch (error) {
      // The photo is stored; viewers fall back to the original until a thumbnail exists.
      console.warn(`thumbnail for ${fileId} not uploaded`, error);
    }
  }
  return fileId;
}
```

A native app or another service can send `Authorization: Bearer <AuthFn session token or API key>` from `getAuthHeaders` instead; bearer requests need no CSRF header.

## What is verified

`npm test --workspace @filefn/docs` typechecks every TypeScript block on this page against the current `@filefn/*`, `authfn`, `@authfn/password`, `@authfn/api-keys`, `@superfunctions/storage-r2` and `@cloudflare/workers-types` declarations, with `src/database.ts` stubbed. It also runs the `src/auth.ts` block with keys created in an in-memory AuthFn database (a key without the needed scope gets 403), and `uploadPhoto` against a stubbed client (an untyped thumbnail uploads nothing). The Worker flow itself (base path, `ctx.waitUntil`, cron cleanup) is exercised in workerd by the `@filefn/server` suite described in [Cloudflare Workers](./cloudflare-workers). Live R2 (including its CORS rule), Queues, Containers and cron on a Cloudflare account are not covered.

# Changelog

Source: https://filefn.com/docs/reference/changelog


Notable filefn releases and migration notes.


# Changelog

filefn follows semver. The `@filefn/server` version is the spine of these notes. Breaking changes are flagged.

## Unreleased

- **Breaking (`@filefn/client` 0.5):** offline uploads go to a durable OPFS queue bound to `offline.partition` (a service and a user or guest namespace). Without a partition, an offline `uploadFile` throws `FILEFN_OFFLINE_PARTITION_REQUIRED`; `offline.currentPrincipal` is also required (it must answer from local state, without a network request), and queued uploads and hooks run only while it returns the partition's principal. Replays with the built-in transport need `offline.getAuthHeaders(principal)` (`FILEFN_OFFLINE_CREDENTIALS_REQUIRED` otherwise) and send only its headers, never with cookies (`credentials: "omit"`); the client's partition (frozen) and transport are captured when its queue is made. A hold stops an upload already running in any tab before its next request. Tabs announce runnable work to each other on a `BroadcastChannel`, and a started `OfflineSync` also polls while idle (`idlePollMs`). The queue journals each generation's replay key, holds, verification and publication; coordinates tabs with `navigator.locks` (or `offline.queue.coordinator`) and refuses durable work without either; and enforces entry and byte limits. Uploads staged by 0.4 and earlier are no longer replayed automatically: migrate them with `OfflineQueue.migrateLegacyUpload` once you can prove whose they are. Sync callbacks, queue listeners and `whenSettled` waiters are checked against `currentPrincipal` before each delivery, so a callback that switches the account receives nothing more of the old principal's. A quota error during `migrateLegacyUpload` is the typed capacity refusal and keeps the legacy upload. Call `client.dispose()` on logout or account switch. See Features › Offline.
- The offline queue confirms a publication only for `undefined` or a plain `{ result?, published?: true }` envelope (a `reconcile` check only for `{ published: true, result? }` or `{ published: false }`; a manual outcome refuses other keys), returns no entry from `process`, `reconcile` or `stage` once a callback switched the account, revokes every preview URL when a principal check fails, reclaims safe data and retries once when the browser runs out of quota during a stage, and disposes the syncs driving a queue when that queue is disposed (`queue.onDispose`). An `upload/init` replay that reports an ended session with a malformed session ID stays ambiguous under the same key. A verifier decides only with an exact `{ verified: true }` or `{ verified: false, reason? }` envelope. `get`, `list` and `migrateLegacyUpload` fence their results on the principal like `process`, `whenSettled` waiters a read settles settle only after that read returned, and no preview URL is created after a principal switch during its read. The pending-local preview is the highest generation of the file, not the entry written last. A hold or principal switch that stops a completed-session read-back uses no attempt. Reclamation frees the data of an entry being restaged that never committed a journal, and frees a published entry's data before writing its tombstone.
- `@filefn/client` sends the `upload/init` idempotency key in the `x-idempotency-key` header. It used to send it in the body, which the server ignored. A key must be 1-255 visible ASCII characters (`FILEFN_INVALID_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY` otherwise), and an application retry must pass the same `fileId` as its first call. Offline, each staged generation sends its own key (the caller's key, if any, is its prefix); a guest partition needs `offline.uploader`; `queue.reconcile` outcomes name their `attemptId`.
- `upload/init` also honors an `idempotencyKey` in the JSON body, with a deprecation warning, until the next minor release; a request giving both forms must give the same value. An idempotent replay reports the session's `status`, and a completed session's `fileId` and `versionId`, so a client confirms the stored file instead of uploading again and starts an expired or aborted session again under a new key. A completed session that never recorded its own version reports no `fileId` or `versionId`. A completed replay adds `versionConfirmed: true` while the recorded version is still stored under its file (checked for the session's owner, no read permission needed), and `@filefn/client` settles on it without reading the version back, so a write-only uploader whose completion response was lost is no longer left ambiguous.
- A proxy part upload that finds its session completed by another request meanwhile returns `409 FILEFN_UPLOAD_ALREADY_COMPLETED` (it returned `410 FILEFN_UPLOAD_ABORTED`), and completing a session whose live completion claim outlasts its expiry waits for that completion instead of returning `410 FILEFN_UPLOAD_EXPIRED`. An offline replay starts again under a new key only when `upload/init` reports the session ended, which a replay now does only after moving the session to `expired` with a conditional write that excludes any later completion claim; an expired session an earlier FileFn left partly published is finished as a publication instead. A completion past the expiry whose claim is stale (it crashed) is ended the same way, by `upload/init` or by `upload/complete` (which records the end before returning 410), so the replay reports it ended and starts again under a new key. A session recorded as `expired` refuses part signing, part uploads, part completion and completion with `410 FILEFN_UPLOAD_EXPIRED` on every worker, whatever its clock says.
- Cross-origin hosts must allow the `x-idempotency-key` and `x-filefn-replay-scope` request headers (keyed uploads and every offline replay send them); the framework guides, the Hono quickstart and the production example now list them.
- Offline replays are bound to one account from their first request: the built-in transport marks each `upload/init`, the first included, with `x-filefn-replay-scope` set to the scope of the account the partition expects (`offline.replayAccount(principal)`, by default the partition principal's `principalId` and `tenantId`), and `@filefn/server` refuses a marked init whose caller is unauthenticated or the shared `anonymous` principal (401 `FILEFN_AUTH_REQUIRED`, also where `auth.required` is false) or has another owner or tenant (409 `FILEFN_REPLAY_SCOPE_MISMATCH`), creating nothing; the generation stays provisional under the same key. There is no `unpinned` first init. A response without `replayScope` (a server before 0.8) is ambiguous: the built-in replay needs `@filefn/server` 0.8. Custom uploaders receive `replayScope` and `pinReplayScope`.
- An `in_progress` replay or session status whose completion was decided reports `completionStarted: true`, and `@filefn/client` then signs no part and finishes it with the completion call (an adopted earlier publication no longer loops on part signing); a status read that reports `completed` is reconciled through the same key's replay.
- The offline queue fences every entry-returning call (`migrateLegacyUpload`, `stage` and `hold` included) after its lock coordinator returns; applies an observation only to what existed when it was read (an old read never settles a newer generation's waiter, and a late cancel never aborts or revokes a newer generation); treats a journal or partition file it cannot read as an error rather than an uncommitted remnant (nothing is removed and no generation number is reused); records the destination queue root and entry ID in a legacy admission claim, so another root is refused as `already-migrated`; and goes on with the pass, re-planning the entry, when another tab replaces or cancels the generation being uploaded.
- An explicit failure envelope (`ok` present and not `true`, or an `error`) never confirms anything: not an expired or aborted session at `upload/init` (the key is kept), and not a stored version at completion, at a completed `upload/init`, at the version readback or from a custom `offline.uploader`; the generation stays provisional under the same key. A coded 4xx from a signed storage URL, a same-origin one included, is read as a FileFn error only on FileFn's verified part route, so it stays provisional too. Every queue call that reads or writes the journal (`listLegacyUploads`, `usage`, `reclaim`, `release` and `cancel` included) passes the principal and disposal fence after its lock coordinator returns, for its errors (a generation conflict naming the current generation, say) as well as its results. A legacy migration refused before anything was admitted (`generation-conflict`, `publication-pending`, `capacity`) drops its claim, so a retry may choose a free `entryId`. A preview read that a newer stage, cancel or preview overtook is read again instead of revoking or replacing the newer preview. `stage` refuses a file larger than `maxBytes` before reading it, and an offline `uploadFile` refuses an `idempotencyKey` over 200 characters synchronously.
- Upload init and complete that cannot verify a stored size return `500 FILEFN_STORAGE_STAT_UNAVAILABLE` with the message `Upload size cannot be verified`. A complete whose proxy parts are missing returns `409 FILEFN_UPLOAD_INCOMPLETE` with the message `Upload incomplete`. Neither response names the storage adapter or the upload session.
- A metric sink passed directly in the `observability` configuration receives upload failures (`filefn.upload` / `failure`, with `labels.reason` of `size_unverified`, `parts_missing`, or `size_mismatch`), quota denials (`filefn.quota` / `denied`), and processing duration (`filefn.processing` / `complete`, with `durationMs`). Those labels are a closed set: no file id, session id, error text, or usage figure.
- A processing service built on its own with `createProcessingService` never serves an artifact whose parent file row is missing. `getArtifactDownloadUrl` answers `404 FILEFN_NOT_FOUND` (`Artifact not found`) for it with or without a `readChecker`; before, a service without a `readChecker` signed a URL for it. An artifact whose file row exists is served as before. `createFileFn` always configured a `readChecker`, so it already behaved this way. Standalone hosts that create artifact rows without a `files` row must create the file row first.

## 0.7.0 — security

An unauthenticated caller is the principal `anonymous` and owns nothing. A public upload stays readable and listable by anyone. A private one needs a grant made to `anonymous`. That caller cannot replace or delete the upload, and cannot create, list, or revoke share links or grants. Existing share links and grants on anonymous uploads keep working. Signed-in owners can manage grants for their own files over HTTP. Creating a share link requires a signed-in user with `canShare` on the file. To clean up legacy access on files owned by `anonymous`, set `revokedAt` on unwanted `fileShares` rows for those files and delete unwanted `filePermissions` rows for those files. Never return the principal id `anonymous` from `resolveSession`.

The same release also sanitizes storage keys, checks the stored upload size, tightens artifact keys and download headers, and scopes idempotency to the caller. Init validation, roles, rate limits, owner quota, and log hygiene land here, including the same key, init, and size checks in the Python client.

Packages in this release: `@filefn/server` 0.7.0, `@filefn/processing` 0.4.0, `@filefn/processing-container` 0.2.0, `@filefn/client` 0.4.0, `@filefn/admin` 0.1.1, `@superfunctions/storage-local` 0.3.0, and Python `filefn` 0.2.0.

## 0.6.1

- A completion fences itself against an abort or a duplicate complete of the same session.

## 0.6.0

- Import an object that already exists in storage.
- Processing can run in a container.

## 0.5.0

- A client can supply processing artifacts for a version.

## 0.4.2

- A client can choose the file id at init.
- The client migrates a pending upload onto that id.

## 0.4.1

- Storage keys are per upload session.

## 0.4.0

- Processing runs from a queue, including Cloudflare Queues.

## 0.3.1

- Workers type definitions aligned with the Workers runtime.

## 0.3.0

- Client transport for that runtime.

## 0.2.1

## 0.2.0

## 0.1.1

- Patch release on the initial server.

# Configuration

Source: https://filefn.com/docs/reference/configuration


Every option in FileFnConfig — types, defaults, and effects.


# Configuration

`createFileFn(config: FileFnConfig)` accepts a single options object.

## Required

| Field | Type | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | `Adapter` | The DB adapter (`@superfunctions/db`); `db` remains a deprecated alias. |
| `storage` | `StorageAdapter` | The storage adapter (`@superfunctions/storage`). |

## Policies

| Field | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `policies` | `Policy[]` | `[]` | Initial policies. Use `createNucleusPolicies()` for sensible defaults. |

Policies can also be added at runtime via `fileFn.definePolicy(name, policy)`.

## Auth

| Field | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `auth.resolveSession` | `(req: Request) => Promise<Principal | null>` | undefined | Resolves the calling principal. |
| `auth.required` | `boolean` | `false` | When true, anonymous requests fail with `FILEFN_AUTH_REQUIRED`. |

## Authorizer

| Field | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `authorizer` | `Authorizer` | `createDefaultAuthorizer({ db, namespace })` | Custom permission resolution. |

Default authorizer reads `filefn_file_permissions` and respects ownership.

## Quota

| Field | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `quota` | `QuotaProvider` | undefined | Optional storage-quota gate on `init`. |

## Rate limiting

| Field | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rateLimiter` | `RateLimiter` | undefined | Single global rate limiter. |
| `stores` | `RuntimeStores` | undefined | Shared `atomicKv` / `kv` stores. |
| `rateLimit.mode` | `"strict" \| "best-effort" \| "local"` | inferred from stores | Strict requires CAS-capable `stores.atomicKv`; best-effort uses `stores.kv`; local keeps counters in-process. |
| `rateLimit.algorithm` | `"fixed-window" | "sliding-window" | "token-bucket"` | `"fixed-window"` | Algorithm. |
| `rateLimit.limits.uploadInit` | `{ windowSeconds, maxRequests }` | undefined | Per-route. |
| `rateLimit.limits.uploadSign` | same | undefined | |
| `rateLimit.limits.uploadComplete` | same | undefined | |
| `rateLimit.limits.download` | same | undefined | |
| `rateLimit.limits.shareDownload` | same | undefined | |
| `rateLimit.limits.artifactDownload` | same | undefined | |

## Multipart

| Field | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultChunkSizeBytes` | `number` | `5 * 1024 * 1024` | Floor for chunk size. |
| `uploadSessionTtlSeconds` | `number` | `86400` | Session lifetime. |
| `signedUrlTtlSeconds` | `number` | `900` | Per-part signed URL lifetime. |

## Capabilities

| Field | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dedup.enabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Content-addressable storage. |
| `processing.enabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Run processors after upload. |
| `processing.processors` | `Processor[]` | `[]` | Processors to register. |
| `processing.flowFn` | `FlowFnProvider` | undefined | Queue provider for async processing; FileFn enqueues on `getQueue("filefn.processing")`. |

## Misc

| Field | Type | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `namespace` | `string` | `"filefn"` | Table prefix. |
| `basePath` | `string` | root | Serve every route under this prefix, e.g. `"/files"`; invalid values throw `FILEFN_BASE_PATH_INVALID`. |
| `runtime.defer` | `(work: Promise<unknown>) => void` | detached `setImmediate` | Keeps background work alive past the response, e.g. `ctx.waitUntil`. |
| `observability` | `ObservabilityInput<FileFnObservationEvent>` | undefined | Structured logger, events, metrics, traces and request observations. |

## Example: production config

```ts
const fileFn = createFileFn({
  database: createPostgresAdapter({ pool }),
  storage: createS3Storage({ region, bucket, cdnPrefix }),
  policies: createNucleusPolicies(),

  auth: {
    resolveSession: async (req) => {
      const session = await authFn.getSession(req);
      return session ? { principalId: session.userId, tenantId: session.tenantId } : null;
    },
    required: true,
  },

  quota: storageQuotaProvider,
  authorizer: composeAuthorizers([orgAdminCanRead, createDefaultAuthorizer({ db, namespace: "filefn" })]),
  observability: { logger: pinoLogger },
  stores: { atomicKv: redisAtomicStore },

  rateLimit: {
    mode: "strict",
    algorithm: "sliding-window",
    limits: {
      uploadInit:        { windowSeconds: 60, maxRequests: 10 },
      uploadSign:        { windowSeconds: 60, maxRequests: 600 },
      uploadComplete:    { windowSeconds: 60, maxRequests: 30 },
      download:          { windowSeconds: 60, maxRequests: 120 },
      shareDownload:     { windowSeconds: 60, maxRequests: 60 },
      artifactDownload:  { windowSeconds: 60, maxRequests: 600 },
    },
  },

  defaultChunkSizeBytes: 5 * 1024 * 1024,
  uploadSessionTtlSeconds: 86400,
  signedUrlTtlSeconds: 900,

  dedup: { enabled: true },

  processing: {
    enabled: true,
    processors: [
      createThumbnailProcessor({ sizes: [{ name: "thumb", width: 256 }, { name: "preview", width: 1024 }] }),
      createPdfPreviewProcessor({ sizes: [{ name: "preview", width: 1024 }] }),
    ],
    flowFn: queueProvider,
  },
});
```

## See also

- [SDKs › Server](../sdk/server) — annotated API.

# Envelopes

Source: https://filefn.com/docs/reference/envelopes


The success and error wrapper every filefn route returns.


# Envelopes

Every filefn JSON response uses one of two envelopes.

## Success

```jsonc
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": { /* ... payload ... */ }
}
```

The shape of `data` varies per route. See [Routes](./routes) for per-endpoint shapes.

Examples:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": {
    "uploadSessionId": "ups_2cd9...",
    "uploadMode": "multipart-signed-url",
    "chunkSizeBytes": 5242880,
    "totalParts": 12,
    "storageKey": "tenant-acme/images/file_xxx/version_yyy/avatar.png",
    "expiresAt": "2026-05-22T11:30:00Z",
    "uploadSessionToken": "upls_live_...",
    "fileId": "file_xxx"
  }
}
```

## Error

```jsonc
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "FILEFN_POLICY_NOT_FOUND",
    "message": "Policy 'public-image' not found",
    "details": { "policy": "public-image" }
  }
}
```

`code` is the canonical `FILEFN_*` string. `message` is human-readable. `details` is optional structured context (always JSON-safe).

## HTTP semantics

- 2xx → `{ ok: true, data }`.
- 4xx / 5xx → `{ ok: false, error }`.
- The HTTP status code is *also* the `error.status` field — clients can switch on either.

## Streaming responses

Routes that stream binary content (download proxy, share download proxy, artifact download proxy) don't use envelopes. They return raw bytes with appropriate `Content-Type` and `Content-Disposition` headers.

## Custom errors

If you implement a custom `Authorizer` or `QuotaProvider` and want to throw a typed error, throw `FileFnError`:

```ts
import { FileFnError, ErrorCodes } from "@filefn/server";

throw new FileFnError(
  ErrorCodes.FORBIDDEN,
  "Cross-tenant access denied",
  403,
  { fileId, tenantId, principalTenantId }
);
```

The kernel converts it to the standard error envelope. Other thrown values become `FILEFN_INTERNAL_ERROR` with the original message redacted.

## Type-safe consumption

```ts
import type { FileFnEnvelope } from "@filefn/server";

type Envelope<T> =
  | { ok: true;  data: T }
  | { ok: false; error: { code: string; message: string; details?: Record<string, unknown> } };
```

`@filefn/client` already unwraps envelopes for you — every method returns the success payload or throws `FileFnHttpError`.

## See also

- [Errors](./errors) — the error code reference.


---

# Errors

Source: https://filefn.com/docs/reference/errors


Every filefn error code with its HTTP status, message, common causes, and fixes.


# Errors

Every filefn error is a `FileFnError` with:

```ts
{
  code: string;          // "FILEFN_POLICY_NOT_FOUND"
  message: string;       // human-readable
  status: number;        // HTTP status
  details?: object;      // structured context
}
```

Wire-format envelope:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "FILEFN_POLICY_NOT_FOUND",
    "message": "Policy 'public-image' not found",
    "details": { "policy": "public-image" }
  }
}
```

## Auth and access

| Code | HTTP | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FILEFN_AUTH_REQUIRED` | 401 | `auth.required: true` and no session resolved. | Sign in; ensure auth wiring forwards cookies / `Authorization`. |
| `FILEFN_FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Authorizer denied. On upload, the `fileId` names a file the caller cannot write: at init when the file exists, or at completion when another principal created it first (the session is then aborted, so a retry returns `FILEFN_UPLOAD_ABORTED`, and its bytes are deleted, by the expired-session cleanup if a delete fails). | Check ownership / grants; check the principal is in the right tenant. |
| `FILEFN_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | File / artifact / share / permission not found. | Confirm the id exists; remember anti-enumeration: 404 may mask a permission denial. |
| `FILEFN_SESSION_TOKEN_REQUIRED` | 401 | Anonymous upload missing `x-upload-session-token`. | Pass the token returned from `POST /upload/init`. |
| `FILEFN_SESSION_TOKEN_INVALID` | 403 | Wrong token for the session. | Re-init the upload, or check storage in the client. |

## Policy

| Code | HTTP | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FILEFN_POLICY_NOT_FOUND` | 400 | Policy name doesn't exist. | Pre-define the policy with `fileFn.definePolicy` or `policies` config. |
| `FILEFN_POLICY_CONTENT_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED` | 400 | MIME doesn't match `policy.contentTypes`. | Add the MIME or pick a different policy. |
| `FILEFN_POLICY_MAX_SIZE_EXCEEDED` | 400 | File bigger than `policy.maxSizeBytes`. | Bump the policy or split the upload. |

## Quota and limits

| Code | HTTP | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FILEFN_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` | 402 | `QuotaProvider.check` denied. | Surface plan info to the user; let them upgrade or delete. |
| `FILEFN_RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Per-route rate limit hit. | Retry after `details.resetAt`. |

## Multipart

| Code | HTTP | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FILEFN_INVALID_PART_NUMBER` | 400 | `partNumber < 1` or `> totalParts`. | Use the part numbers returned by init. |
| `FILEFN_INVALID_ETAG` | 400 | etag empty or malformed. | Read `ETag` from the storage PUT response and pass it through. |
| `FILEFN_UPLOAD_INCOMPLETE` | 409 | `complete` called before all parts are recorded, or a recorded proxy part object is missing. The message is `Upload incomplete` and does not include the session id. | Record every part, and keep the part objects, before `complete`. |
| `FILEFN_UPLOAD_EXPIRED` | 410 | Session past TTL. | Call `init` again with a new idempotency key. |
| `FILEFN_UPLOAD_ABORTED` | 410 | Session was aborted. | Same — start a new session. |
| `FILEFN_UPLOAD_COMPLETION_IN_PROGRESS` | 409 | On `complete`: another completion call of the same upload session (in any FileFn process sharing the database), or the commit step of a completion of the same `fileId` in the same database in this process, is still running and did not finish within 30 seconds. On `abort` or a part call: a completion of the session is running or publishing (a completion call finishes it). On `DELETE /:fileId`: an upload session of the file is completing or publishing. Nothing was changed; `details.retryable` is `true`. | Retry `POST /upload/:id/complete` after a short delay; it returns the completed result. An abort cannot end a session whose completion is running. |
| `FILEFN_UPLOAD_ALREADY_COMPLETED` | 409 | `complete` called twice. | Treat as success; the file id is in the previous response. |
| `FILEFN_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` | 409 | Same idempotency key + different request body. | Use a new idempotency key, or replay with the same body. |
| `FILEFN_PART_CONFLICT` | 409 | Same part recorded with a different etag. | Check for concurrent retries; pick a single canonical etag. |
| `FILEFN_UPLOAD_SIZE_MISMATCH` | 409 | Sum of part sizes ≠ `size` declared at init. | Re-check declared size before init. |
| `FILEFN_NO_SUPPORTED_UPLOAD_MODE` | 500 | Adapter doesn't support multipart and proxy is disabled. | Use a multipart-capable adapter (S3, GCS, R2, MinIO, Azure). |
| `FILEFN_STORAGE_STAT_UNAVAILABLE` | 500 | Init requires a storage adapter that implements `statObject`. Completion returns this code if a required stat cannot verify the uploaded object or its parts. The message is `Upload size cannot be verified`. | Check adapter support and availability, then retry. |
| `FILEFN_STORAGE_PATH_NOT_PER_VERSION` | 500 | The key the policy's `storagePath` returned does not contain the session's full `versionId`, so two upload sessions could write one object. Refused at init before any session row or storage upload is created. | Include the whole `versionId`, unshortened, in the key your `storagePath` returns. |
| `FILEFN_INVALID_FILE_ID` | 400 | The `fileId` sent to `POST /upload/init` does not match `file_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,64}` (or is not a string). Refused before any session row or storage upload is created. | Send an ID in that grammar, such as `generateFileId()` output, or omit `fileId` to let the server generate one. |
| `FILEFN_OFFLINE_UNSUPPORTED` | 400 | Client requested OPFS but the runtime doesn't support it. | Skip OPFS, upload directly. |
| `FILEFN_SESSION_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | The `uploadSessionId` doesn't exist. | Use the id returned from init; sessions expire after TTL. |

## Share links

| Code | HTTP | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FILEFN_SHARE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Token doesn't match any share row. | Token is invalid or revoked. |
| `FILEFN_SHARE_REVOKED` | 410 | Share was revoked. | Surface a "this link is no longer valid" message. |
| `FILEFN_SHARE_EXPIRED` | 410 | Share past `expiresAt`. | Same. |
| `FILEFN_SHARE_DOWNLOADS_EXCEEDED` | 410 | `maxDownloads` exhausted. | Same. |
| `FILEFN_SHARE_DOWNLOAD_CONFLICT` | 409 | Too many concurrent downloads of the link. | Retry. |

## Permissions

| Code | HTTP | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FILEFN_PERMISSION_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | `DELETE` on missing permission id. | Check the id; idempotent delete is safe to skip 404s in your client. |

## Processing

| Code | HTTP | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FILEFN_PROCESSING_ENQUEUE_FAILED` | 503 | The processing queue's `add` rejected. | Check queue health; retry. |
| `FILEFN_INVALID_RENDER_INTENT` | 400 | Unknown render intent. | Use `thumbnail` / `preview` / `full` (or a registered custom intent). |

## See also

- [Routes](./routes) — per-route error matrix.
- [Envelopes](./envelopes) — wire-format details.

# Events

Source: https://filefn.com/docs/reference/events


Every filefn event with its payload, when it fires, and what's redacted.


# Events

filefn emits seven typed events. Subscribe via `fileFn.events.on(name, listener)`.

## Lifecycle

| Event | Fires | Payload (key fields) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `upload.started` | After `POST /upload/init` succeeds. | `uploadSessionId`, `fileName`, `size`, `mimeType`, `policy`, `principalId`, `tenantId` |
| `part.recorded` | After `POST /upload/:id/parts/:n/complete` succeeds. | `uploadSessionId`, `partNumber`, `size` |
| `file:uploaded` | After `POST /upload/:id/complete` succeeds. | `fileId`, `versionId`, `fileName`, `size`, `mimeType`, `ownerId`, `tenantId` |
| `file:deleted` | After `DELETE /:fileId` succeeds. | `fileId`, `ownerId`, `tenantId` |

## Processing

| Event | Fires | Payload (key fields) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `processing.started` | After upload completes; processors begin. | `fileId`, `versionId` |
| `processing.completed` | After all processors finish. For a queued job it is at least once: a delivery that fails or is evicted after the last processor finished, but before the job recorded its completion, leaves the next delivery to emit it; overlapping deliveries of one job can each emit it; a delivery that finds the completion recorded emits nothing. For a queued job, `artifactsCreated` counts the job's artifacts across its deliveries. Artifacts and run rows are still written once per idempotency key. | `fileId`, `versionId`, `artifactsCreated` |
| `processing.failed` | A processor threw / returned `success: false`. For a queued job (`createProcessingJobHandler`), only on the final delivery, once the queue's retries are used up, and never for a job whose file version was deleted (a cleanup of that version's output that fails on the final delivery is logged as an error and not retried). | `fileId`, `versionId`, `error?` |

## Common envelope fields

```ts
interface FileFnEvent {
  type: string;          // "upload.started"
  timestamp: string;     // ISO 8601
  requestId?: string;    // request correlation id
}
```

Plus the per-event payload fields.

## Redaction

The kernel sanitises event payloads before emitting. Tokens, signatures, signed URLs, `Authorization` headers, and live-token strings (`upls_live_*`) are replaced with `[REDACTED]`. You can subscribe to events without worrying about leaking secrets to your logger / queue.

## Wiring

```ts
fileFn.events.on("file:uploaded", (event) => {
  console.log("uploaded", event.fileId, event.versionId);
  // Persist to audit log, kick off downstream pipelines, etc.
});

fileFn.events.on("processing.completed", (event) => {
  if (event.artifactsCreated > 0) {
    invalidateRenderCache(event.fileId);
  }
});

fileFn.events.on("processing.failed", (event) => {
  alertOps({ fileId: event.fileId, error: event.error });
});
```

## Authoring custom events

For domain-specific events (share-clicked, virus-detected, sentiment-scored), emit them from your processors / hooks via your own emitter. The kernel doesn't ship hooks for arbitrary event injection — keep custom events in your own observability layer.

## See also

- [Core Concepts › Events](../core-concepts/events).
- [Core Concepts › Observability](../core-concepts/observability).
